title: SLA-aware pro‑prefill controller with quantile-tier defaults
author: Aisha Thompson
description:
Motivation: Large production workloads showed oscillating unit-econ after applying static prefill defaults. This PR introduces a lightweight controller that selects prefill batch sizes, cache prewarm thresholds, and a quantization tier (int8/4/awq-safe) based on SLA targets (p95 latency) and recent unit-econ signals. The goal is to automate a conservative default that protects latency SLOs while capturing cost savings when the workload permits it.

What this change does: 1) Adds a new controller component (econ/prefill_controller) that consumes short-term telemetry (latency percentiles, token throughput, cache hit rates) and emits a recommended profile object for the serving runtime. 2) Introduces a compact quantile-tier defaults file with three safe profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) that map to vetted quantization and KV cache settings for common model families. 3) Adds a CLI command (redwood econ suggest-profile) that runs a simulated dry-run against the local sampler to produce expected unit-econ deltas. 4) Adds a fallback policy: if latency risk > 5% over target, controller narrows to conservative settings and emits an alert metric. 5) Wiring in telemetry: new econ.profile.recommendation and econ.profile.applied metrics plus a small eval harness to validate quality regression against baseline prompts.

Checklist: - [x] Controller core logic, simulation & safety checks - [x] Quantile-tier defaults and mapping table for Llama-family and Mistral-family - [x] CLI integration and help text - [x] Unit and integration tests for the dry-run simulator - [x] Metrics dashboard sample JSON and Grafana panel template - [x] Documentation in docs/operator/econ-profiles.md - [x] Non-breaking; default controller is opt-in (config flag)

Related: ENG-2481 (unit-econ automation design), ENG-2789 (autoscaling tie-ins). This PR is intentionally conservative in default thresholds and includes a predictable fail-open behavior (fallback to conservative profile plus an alert) to avoid regressions in low-latency products.

Notes on evaluation: In local replay against a 48-hour sample trace, the "balanced" profile yielded ~12% token cost reduction with p95 latency within 1.8% of baseline. Aggressive profile saved ~28% at the cost of p95 regressions in 8% of sampled windows; this is why the default remains balanced and controller requires opt-in in the config.

Merge notes: squash merge. See commits summary and CI checks below.

review_comments: Katherine Lin: Nice shape. A few asks: (1) make the default thresholds editable via ConfigMap; (2) add a small canary window for applying aggressive changes so we can observe regressions before global flip. Also prefer non-blocking logs over raising on sim timeouts.
Author (Aisha): Addressed — thresholds are now configurable via operator config and the applier includes a 10-minute canary window flag. Sim timeouts now emit warn-level logs. PTAL.

Diego Alvarez: Can we add a short note on how this interacts with Dedicated capacity reserved pools? If a customer pins to Dedicated, controller should not change quantization without explicit consent.
Author (Aisha): Added explicit check: controller is a no-op for Dedicated pools unless an admin opt-in label is present. Documented in the operator guide.
Marta Novak: Tests look good; one nit: please use a deterministic seed for trace replay to make CI reproducible.
Author (Aisha): Added deterministic seeding and recorded golden traces used by CI. Marking as ready for merge.
merge_outcome: Merged by Katherine Lin on 2024-11-12 using squash. Commit message consolidated controller + quantile-tier defaults + docs. Backported guidance added to release notes.
release_notes: Opt-in SLA-aware prefill controller and three safe quantization-tier defaults. Adds 'redwood econ suggest-profile' CLI to simulate unit-econ impact. Controller is opt-in and no changes are applied to Dedicated pools without explicit admin consent.
